correctness.rationale: The plane-quartic Jacobian criterion gives smoothness on r≠±2; a bijective cube map over every odd extension yields N1=18, even Weil polynomial and functional-equation reduction to one N2 count. Exhaustive enumeration of all 289 quadratic-field values in two irreducible representations, with two independent cube-count tests, proves the five N2 values. The elliptic quotient V²=U³+(r²−4)/4 has trace zero, so division yields the stated Prym factors; rational irreducibility tests prove four simple surface types. Exact multinomial Hasse coefficients verify Cartier vanishing at ±5 and no other parameters. Geometric isomorphism criterion is explicitly attributed to the primary source.

value.rationale: The exact five-type zeta and four simple Prym surface classification is a complete natural arithmetic invariant of the distinguished order-six genus-three family over the first targeted prime, revealing two pairs of nonisomorphic geometric classes with isogenous Jacobians despite universal N1=18. The elliptic quotient motivates the Prym invariant and the exact N2 census determines all extension counts. It is not merely a new example of a known maximal curve.
